root_cause.text: The driver module unload was allowed to proceed while a fabric scan was still in progress, causing DMA memory to be freed in interrupt context when a work item allocation was skipped due to the UNLOADING flag being set.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "The root cause of this was that there was a free (dma_free_attrs) in the interrupt context. There was a device discovery/fabric scan in progress. A module unload was issued which set the UNLOADING flag. As part of the discovery, after receiving an interrupt a work queue was scheduled (which involved a work to be queued). Since the UNLOADING flag is set, the work item was not allocated and the mapped memory had to be freed. The free occurred in interrupt context leading to system crash." The patch adds `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)` to the wait condition in `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` to delay unload until scan completes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready waits until any scan is complete before declaring the HBA ready.
intent_record.what: Added an additional condition to the while loop in qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready to also wait while the SF_SCANNING flag is set in vha->scan.scan_flags.
intent_record.how: The function now waits until any ongoing scan (indicated by SF_SCANNING) is complete before proceeding, preventing premature return during scan activity.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready waits until any scan is complete before declaring the HBA ready.

relevance_review.reason: The change ensures that the HBA is not declared ready until any ongoing scan completes, which prevents the module unload from proceeding while a scan is still in progress, thus directly addressing the root cause of the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: Breaks the wait loop when UNLOADING flag is set, allowing the function to return before the fabric scan is complete, thus permitting module unload to proceed while a scan is still in progress.
Condition that triggers the premature break, skipping the remaining wait for scan completion.
Part of the loop condition that only checks for a specific scan type (FX00_TARGET_SCAN), missing the general fabric scan flag, so the loop may exit even if a fabric scan is ongoing.
Part of the loop condition that does not include a check for fabric scan in progress, contributing to the loop's failure to wait for scan completion.
The overall loop condition lacks any check for a fabric scan being active, so the loop can exit before the scan is complete, especially when combined with the UNLOADING break.
